name: Tagalog (Filipino)
variant: Tagalog (Filipino) of Manila, standard modern spelling
script: Latin (28-letter Filipino alphabet, with ñ and ng), left to right
basis: First-year university Filipino: self and greetings with ang pronouns and markers, family with the na / -ng linker, community with gusto / ayaw and prices, then -um-, mag-, -in verbs and aspect (SEASSI 1st-year Filipino and Oxnard College FILI R101 outline)
src: SEASSI 2025 (University of Wisconsin), Filipino 1st-year syllabus: weekly topics and grammar
Oxnard College, FILI R101 Elementary Filipino 1 course outline (content list; texts include Barrios, Tagalog for Beginners, and Domingo, Elementary Tagalog)
Polyglottist Language Academy, Tagalog Beginner 1 syllabus (weekly topics and grammar)
note: The opening order (greetings, self-introduction, ang pronouns and markers, may / mayroon / wala, then family with the linker, then places, prices, ordering food, gusto / ayaw, then directions and commands with huwag) follows SEASSI and Polyglottist. The list of verb affixes (-um-, mag-, -in), the aspects, particles, po / ho and comparison come from the Oxnard outline, which gives content but not an order; placing verbs in stage 3 and the order inside it is my own judgment and common course practice.
hardest: Verb focus: the affix (-um-, mag-, -in) shows which noun is marked by ang
Aspect, not tense: completed, ongoing and contemplated forms built by affixes and repeating a syllable (kumain, kumakain, kakain)
Three marker sets for nouns and pronouns: ang / ng / sa (ako, ko, akin)
The glottal stop and stress that change meaning but are not shown in normal spelling

items: Sounds and spelling: ng, the glottal stop, and stress that changes meaning
Greetings and respect: Magandang umaga, Kumusta?, po and opo
ang pronouns: ako, ikaw / ka, siya, kami, tayo, kayo, sila
Introducing yourself: Ako si…, Taga-… ako, Taga-saan ka?
ito, iyan, iyon: this and that; Ano ito?
Markers: ang / si, ng / ni, sa / kay
Questions: ba, sino, ano, saan, kailan
Yes and no: oo / opo, hindi / hindi po
Numbers: isa, dalawa, tatlo and the Spanish numbers (uno, dos) used for money and time
may, mayroon / meron, wala: there is, have
The linker na / -ng and ma- adjectives: magandang bahay, bahay na malaki
ng pronouns and possession: ko, mo, niya (bahay ko)
Family and jobs: nanay, tatay, ate, kuya, anak
sa pronouns and place: sa akin, dito, diyan, doon, nasaan
mag- verbs (actor focus): magluto, maglaro, magtrabaho
Aspect: completed, ongoing, contemplated (kumain, kumakain, kakain)
gusto, ayaw, kailangan, puwede: like, don't want, need, can
-in verbs (object focus): kainin, lutuin (Kinain ko ang mangga)
Ordering food and prices: Magkano?, Pabili po, isa pa
Time and days: Anong oras na?, alas-tres, Lunes, kahapon, bukas
Directions and transport: kaliwa, kanan, diretso, jeep
Particles: na, pa, rin / din, lang, naman
